title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidates CI workflows for lint, test and release; improves caching/matrix parallelism to reduce CI time and cost. No change to runtime behavior.
description: Motivation: our CI has accumulated many overlapping workflows (lint/test/release) across multiple repos and actions that cause redundant runs, long queue times, and cache churn. This PR consolidates the lint, unit/integration test, and release automation into a small set of unified workflows, standardizes job naming and annotations, and improves cache/matrix configuration to reduce duplicate work. Goals: 1) reduce CI run count and build minutes, 2) make release automation more deterministic, 3) simplify workflow maintenance and onboarding. Summary of changes: - New workflows/.github/workflows/ci-unified.yml that combines lint, unit, integration tests, and release gating into composable reusable workflows and called workflows. - Split heavy integration tests into a conditional matrix keyed on changed components to avoid running all integration suites on every PR. - Introduced a deterministic cache key scheme for node_modules and actions cache to reduce misses and improve parallel restore. - Tuned matrix parallelism for lint/test jobs to avoid saturating runners and to improve cache locality. - Removed legacy workflows: .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml (kept as references in docs/ci/ for historical context). Checklist: - [x] Add unified workflow and refactors - [x] Migrate repository-specific job definitions into reusable workflow templates - [x] Validate reproducible release job runs in a dry-run repo - [x] Update README and docs/ci/ with new developer guidance - [x] Run infra smoke tests against staging CI runs Implementation notes: the unified workflow uses reusable workflows and composite actions where appropriate. We reduced redundant npm install phases by centralizing dependency install into a cacheable job and passing artifacts between jobs using artifacts and workspace actions when needed. We intentionally keep the release job gated behind a manual approval step and a semantic-release check to preserve current release semantics. Migration plan: remove legacy workflows after 2 weeks of running unified workflows; if regressions found, revert to the stable legacy pipeline via a hotfix branch. The description above is intentionally concise and intended for reviewers and infra owners.
